A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SEELE framework, task-inversion technique, and ReS dataset. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original subject-repositioning experiments, inpainting and outpainting results in Tables 1–3, and qualitative component ablations in its appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and additionally reports a LoRA baseline and a ReS user-preference study in Table 1.

M1.justification: The diffusion backbone, task prompts, mask-generation procedures, harmonization objective and LoRA integration remain unchanged. Segmentation, depth estimation, matting, and shadow handling are retained. Shortened descriptions do not establish changes to the implemented procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use MSCOCO and iHarmony4 for training, ReS for repositioning, Places2 for inpainting, and Flickr-Scenery for outpainting. ReS retains the same image-pair coverage and bidirectional evaluation. The new preference study evaluates retained task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds SDlora, a LoRA-fine-tuned Stable Diffusion comparator, to the ReS comparison. The three existing SD prompt variants and SEELE variants using ZITS++, MAE-FAR, LaMa, and MAT remain. Inpainting and outpainting comparator sets are unchanged.

E3.justification: The principal ReS evaluation changes from PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS to LPIPS plus human preferences for quality and visual consistency. v2 introduces 100 anonymous surveys and top-1 preference proportions, substantially changing the evaluation design. Existing image resizing, training budgets, and dataset splits remain.

E4.justification: v1's small SAM-everything visualization and accompanying examination of segmentation behavior in Appendix A.8 and Figure 12 are removed. The opposite-prompt, harmonization, and preprocessing/postprocessing component ablations are retained in v2 Figures 7–9. The new failure discussion adds interpretation rather than new failure experiments.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for its results. The new survey count describes the evaluation sample, not repeated training runs or uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v2 Table 1 adds SDlora's LPIPS of 0.162 and preference results for nine methods; SEELE leads quality and consistency with 0.290 and 0.329. Existing ReS LPIPS values are unchanged, but PSNR/SSIM results disappear, including MAE-FAR's PSNR advantage over SEELE, 20.453 versus 20.100. Standard benchmark values mostly undergo rounding, although SEELE's outpainting PSNR changes from 15.989 to 16.00, an unexplained discrepancy beyond ordinary two-decimal rounding.

T1.justification: Equations 1 and 2 and the additive LoRA formulation with scale values zero and one are retained. No new mathematical assumptions, derivations, proofs, or formal results appear.

C1.justification: The central SEELE, task-inversion, and ReS contributions remain. v2's introduction newly specifies functionality beyond Magic Editor, including occlusion/perspective preservation and local harmonization, and frames SubRep as operating without explicit scene understanding. v1 instead states a broad aim of matching or surpassing Magic Editor's performance.

C2.justification: v2 adds an overfitting explanation for SDlora's results and a component-specific failure discussion. Semantic inconsistency changes from being beyond scope in v1 to something removal/completion address in v2. Appendix Section 14 adds misuse concerns and planned image labeling; the central manual-mask and amodal-mask limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 identifies the qualitative SD comparator as the simple-prompt variant. However, it omits v1's larger-mask filtering and iterative SAM-refinement details, plus the explicit single-mask construction for alternative inpainting baselines. Core hyperparameters, hardware, LoRA integration instructions, and project/dataset access links remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds Zheng et al. (2021) on scene decomposition and Schuhmann et al. (2022) on LAION-5B. These support revised positioning relative to scene understanding and discussion of training-data scale. Existing related-work categories and most cited works remain.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites and condenses the introduction, introduces the SubRep abbreviation, separates task/dataset description from the SEELE framework, and integrates previously appended evaluation, ablation, and limitation material into the main narrative. Appendix organization and author text also change.

P2.justification: v2 changes typography, margins, running headers, and title/abstract arrangement. It merges user-input/dataset figures, task-inversion/mask figures, and prompt/harmonization ablations; restructures and relocates tables; duplicates the component-ablation display; and removes the SAM visualization. Several retained displays become substantially smaller, particularly the merged ablations and appendix examples.

improvement.justification: The added SDlora comparison and ReS preference study strengthen support for learned-prompt adaptation and perceptual usefulness. Bringing quantitative results and ablations into the main text also improves accessibility. These gains are limited by sparse survey reporting, removal of PSNR/SSIM evidence showing comparator tradeoffs, and losses in implementation detail and figure readability.
